question.problem:
A factory spends  $C(x)=0.002375{x}^{2}+0.3x+1\,000$ dollars to manufacture $x$ units of a certain product. The factory sells the product for $30-\frac{x}{100}$ dollars per unit. Given that the factory can produce at most $2\,000$ units per year, how many units should the factory produce per year to maximize its annual profit?

The optimal number of production is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we apply the candidates test.

First, note that for selling $x$ units of the product per year, the factory has an annual revenue (income) of $R(x)=(30-\frac{x}{100})\cdot x=30x-0.01{x}^{2}$ dollars.

Therefore, the profit function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & =R(x)-C(x) \\  & =30x-0.01{x}^{2}-(0.002375{x}^{2}+0.3x+1\,000) \\  & =-1\,000+29.7x-0.012375{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We note that the permitted domain is $0\le x\le 2\,000.$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $0<x<2\,000.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=29.7-0.02475x.
$$

Solving ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 29.7-0.02475x & =0 \\ x & =1\,200\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $x=1\,200$ lies in the interval $0<x<2\,000.$ All that's left now is to confirm that $x=1\,200$ does indeed give a maximum value of $P(x).$ To do this, we compute the second derivative:   

$$
{P}^{″}(x)=-0.02475<0.
$$

Since the second derivative is negative, the point $x=1\,200$ is indeed a  maximum of $P(x).$ 

Our candidates are $x=0,$ $x=1\,200,$ and $x=2\,000.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =-1\,000 \\ P(1\,200) & =-1\,000+29.7(1\,200)-0.012375(1\,200)^{2}=16\,820\,✓ \\ P(2\,000) & =-1\,000+29.7(2\,000)-0.012375(2\,000)^{2}=9\,500\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the factory will have a maximum annual profit when it produces $1\,200$ units per year.
